scenario: A law-enforcement agency selects negotiators who demonstrate high emotional regulation OR advanced strategic deception detection. These abilities are independent in the candidate population; OR-gate selection creates a negative collider bias in the selected cohort.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (emotional regulation) OR (strategic deception detection)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(emotional_regulation | ¬deception_detection, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(emotional_regulation | deception_detection, selected) and show it equals P(emotional_regulation). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between emotional regulation and strategic deception detection.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks strategic deception detection must possess emotional regulation to be admitted — hence P(emotional_regulation|¬deception_detection,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has strategic deception detection is admitted regardless of emotional regulation, so P(emotional_regulation|deception_detection,sel)=P(emotional_regulation)=0.41. The gap (1.0 vs 0.41) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between emotional regulation and strategic deception detection observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.41+0.49-0.41×0.49=0.6991. (2) Among candidates without strategic deception detection: only those with emotional regulation are selected → P(emotional_regulation|¬deception_detection,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with strategic deception detection: selected regardless of emotional regulation → P(emotional_regulation|deception_detection,sel)=P(emotional_regulation)=0.41. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬deception_detection raises P(emotional_regulation) from 0.41 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.41,0.49
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6991)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.41)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
